title: Determine Duplicate Subtrees

content.problemStatement:
With the `root` of a binary tree, output all **duplicate subtrees**.

For each kind of duplicate subtrees, you only need to output the root node of any **one** of them.

Two trees are **duplicate** if they have the **same structure** with the **same node values**.

**Example 1:**

![](https://assets.leetcode.com/uploads/2020/08/16/e1.jpg)

```
Input: root = [1,2,3,4,null,2,4,null,null,4]
Output: [[2,4],[4]]
```

**Example 2:**

![](https://assets.leetcode.com/uploads/2020/08/16/e2.jpg)

```
Input: root = [2,1,1]
Output: [[1]]
```

**Example 3:**

![](https://assets.leetcode.com/uploads/2020/08/16/e33.jpg)

```
Input: root = [2,2,2,3,null,3,null]
Output: [[2,3],[3]]
```

**Constraints:**

* The number of the nodes in the tree will be in the range `[1, 5000]`
* `-200 <= Node.val <= 200`
constraints: Time complexity must be optimized to run within execution limits.
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [arg1, arg2, ...]

code.Python3:
# Time:  O(n)
# Space: O(n)

import collections


class Solution(object):
    def findDuplicateSubtrees(self, root):
        """
        :type root: TreeNode
        :rtype: List[TreeNode]
        """
        def getid(root, lookup, trees):
            if not root:
                return -1
            node_id = lookup[root.val,
                             getid(root.left, lookup, trees),
                             getid(root.right, lookup, trees)]
            trees[node_id].append(root)
            return node_id

        trees = collections.defaultdict(list)
        lookup = collections.defaultdict()
        lookup.default_factory = lookup.__len__
        getid(root, lookup, trees)
        return [roots[0] for roots in trees.itervalues() if len(roots) > 1]
